# Clover

> Clover is an AI Orchestration Framework connecting real-world Context, human Direction, AI-driven Action, and validated Success into a repeatable cycle. It sits on top of the systems an organization already runs — nothing to install, nothing to migrate onto.

Clover is a framework for reasoning about and governing AI-enabled work, not a mandatory process. Its foundational priority is **System → Human → AI**: the system grounds reality; humans establish purpose, Direction, and accountability; AI provides capability and determines how work happens within human Direction.

The framework has four operational stages: **Context → Direction → Action → Success**. Context is the relevant evidence about system reality needed for the current work. Direction is the human-defined outcome, priorities, constraints, boundaries, and accountability. Action is AI determining and executing the path within that Context and Direction. Success is the intended outcome demonstrated by evidence from the real system or environment.

What makes Clover distinct is the relationship between those four stages and the authority boundary around them. The claim is testable: context should become more inspectable, Direction more explicit, execution safely delegable where evidence supports it, and Success harder to claim without environmental evidence tied to the intended outcome. A team should keep Clover only where applying it improves observable work.

**Capability may scale. Direction remains human.** Competitive pressure or stronger models may increase delegated execution inside Action. They do not transfer purpose, acceptable risk, priorities, boundaries, or accountability to AI.

Delegated execution is an engineering decision. Consider evidence from comparable outcomes, blast radius, observability, reversibility, and approval boundaries. **Delegation can move work. It does not move Direction.**

A failed result returns the cycle to Context with new information. The goal is not to retry the same Action on the same evidence.

Growth is not a fifth operational stage. It is the learning that can emerge when the four stages repeat and useful learning is preserved. Growth can accumulate across humans, AI systems, the system being worked on, teams, organizations, and frontier AI development; these layers are controlled differently. Clover does not assume customer work trains an AI provider's underlying model.

## Pages

- [The framework](https://cloverframework.com/): the full argument and the four-stage cycle.
- [Getting started](https://cloverframework.com/start/): read-only system access, AGENTS.md, and a first cycle.
- [Security and governance](https://cloverframework.com/security/): access, attribution, approvals, agent behavior, and delegated execution.
- [Evidence](https://cloverframework.com/evidence/): case studies and reference implementations, each stating where it stopped.
- [Glossary](https://cloverframework.com/glossary/): plain-language definitions.
- [The author](https://cloverframework.com/author/): who wrote it.

## Core

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/AGENTS.md): Instructions for agents — stages, evidence rules, authority boundaries, failure checks, and context handoff.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/README.md): What Clover is, what makes it distinct, the four stages, adoption, and limits.
- [The four stages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/04-framework.md): The framework, distinction, delegated execution, and evaluation model.
- [Principles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/03-principles.md): One principle per stage, including the human Direction boundary.

## Putting it into practice

- [The orchestration environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/orchestration-environment.md): The access layer that feeds Context — what to connect, how to grant access safely, and a build sequence ordered by increasing risk.
- [Context engineering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/05-context-engineering.md): Why context matters and where persistent context files should live.
- [Adoption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/09-adoption.md): How to test whether Clover changes observable work.
- [Governance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/08-governance.md): Ownership, approval, attribution, access, and delegated execution.
- [Success in practice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/07-success.md): What counts as evidence of the intended outcome.
- [Quickstart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/QUICKSTART.md): First cycle in about 15 minutes.
- [Orchestration brief template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/templates/orchestration-brief.md): One-page working artifact covering all four stages.

- [Reference implementations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/santhoshsathish94/clover-framework/main/docs/reference-implementations.md): Patterns for system access and AI-enabled work.
